score_100.reason: Fig. 5C compares the proportions of response types among granule cell-odor pairs under Task and Passive conditions. The core is to understand the negative finding that response proportions are similar and to interpret it together with later response-amplitude differences as gain modulation rather than recruitment modulation. The graph consists of two side-by-side pie charts and is worth 30 points. The analysis unit, cell-odor pair, and the classification criteria are worth 20 points. The scientific interpretation is split into two items: similar response-type proportions and unchanged recruitment are worth 25 points, and the gain-modulation mechanism supported by similar proportions plus stronger amplitudes is worth 25 points. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, analysis unit 20, similar-proportion conclusion 25, gain-modulation interpretation 25.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 5C shows that the proportions of odor-excited, odor-suppressed, and non-responsive granule cell-odor pairs are similar under Task and Passive conditions. In the Task condition, the proportions are about 26.1% excited, 20.2% suppressed, and 53.7% non-responsive; in the Passive condition, they are about 24.3% excited, 16.5% suppressed, and 59.2% non-responsive. The core conclusion is that task engagement does not primarily alter olfactory representation by recruiting more odor-responsive cell-odor pairs. Instead, when interpreted together with later response-amplitude enhancement, it supports gain modulation: the response amplitude of already responsive cell-odor pairs is amplified while response proportions remain largely unchanged.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes two side-by-side pie charts, with the Task condition on the left and the Passive condition on the right, using different colors for Excited, Suppressed, and Non-responsive response classes; slice proportions are close to the original figure and clearly show that response-type proportions are broadly similar across the two conditions.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the panel is misidentified as a bar plot, scatter plot, time series, heatmap, or single-cell trace. Deduct 12 points if either the Task or Passive pie chart is missing. Deduct 10 points if the three response classes are not distinguished. Deduct 12 points if the proportions are directionally wrong, for example if responsive categories are shown as the overwhelming majority. Deduct 6 points if the proportional relationship is not compared with the original figure.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states that the analysis unit is a cell-odor pair, meaning the combination of each granule cell with each odor, rather than individual cells alone; the Excited, Suppressed, and Non-responsive classification criteria are kept consistent between Task and Passive conditions, and both groups come from 4 mice.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the analysis unit is misdescribed as individual cells rather than cell-odor pairs. Deduct 6 points if the consistency of classification criteria across the two conditions is not stated. Deduct 5 points if the sample source or mouse count for the Task and Passive groups is clearly wrong. Deduct 12 points if the analysis unit is not explained at all.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the core negative finding that response-type proportions are similar across the two conditions, meaning task engagement does not substantially change the fraction of odor-excited, odor-suppressed, and non-responsive cell-odor pairs; recruitment of responsive cell-odor pairs is largely unchanged, and this panel shows fraction rather than response amplitude.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 18 points if the Task condition is claimed to recruit many more responsive cell-odor pairs. Deduct 8 points if the response does not distinguish fraction from response amplitude. Deduct 10 points if percentages are reported without explaining unchanged recruitment. Deduct 8 points if similar proportions are interpreted as task having no effect at all on olfactory processing.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains that similar proportions together with enhanced response amplitudes support a gain-modulation mechanism: task engagement enhances olfactory processing mainly by amplifying responses of already odor-responsive cell-odor pairs rather than by recruiting additional responsive units; this interpretation is consistent with the role of cholinergic modulation in increasing olfactory-bulb processing gain.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 12 points if gain modulation is not discussed. Deduct 15 points if the result is interpreted as recruitment modulation. Deduct 8 points if the response does not state that the panel should be interpreted together with response-amplitude enhancement. Deduct 10 points if similar proportions are claimed to mean there is no task modulation.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe cell-odor pair as neuron-odor pair or cell-odor pairing.
It is acceptable to describe excited, suppressed, and non-responsive as excitatory, inhibitory/suppressed, and non-responsive classes.
Percentages may be approximate as long as the similarity between Task and Passive is preserved.
It is acceptable to describe unchanged recruitment as unchanged response-cell fraction or no increase in responsive units.
It is acceptable to describe gain modulation as response-amplitude amplification or gain enhancement.
It is acceptable to describe the Passive condition as passive odor exposure.
It is not necessary to provide all numerical details from Fig. 5D, as long as it is correctly described as showing amplitude changes.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the Task and Passive pie charts, explaining that the analysis unit is a cell-odor pair, accurately stating that response-type proportions are similar across conditions, and interpreting the negative finding together with response-amplitude enhancement as gain modulation rather than recruitment modulation. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the graph and direction of similar proportions are correct but the analysis unit, fraction/amplitude distinction, or mechanism interpretation is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is confused with a response-amplitude plot, similar proportions are misread as large recruitment changes, or the gain-modulation meaning is not explained.
